Cc: Mai Patel <mai.patel@spectrahealth.com>, procurement <procurement@spectrahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TIA scope and subprocessor carveouts – initial materials attached

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the call this morning. I promised to send over the baseline materials so your team can scope the evidence sprint. Attached: Spectra_TIA_Scope.xlsx and Subprocessor-Inventory_Spectra.csv.

Two quick asks from our side:
- We have three small analytics subprocessors in APAC that have contractual restrictions — would Redwood accept a TIA carveout for those (i.e., exclude them from UK IDTA transit requirements) while keeping standard SCCs for the rest?
- Can you confirm whether the SCC + UK IDTA approach is still the preferred default for Redwood-hosted deployments, or do we need to plan for a separate onshore-fallback/residency addendum?

We’re hoping to align on a mutual action plan (timeline + evidence gate) so procurement can proceed with the legal redline.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Head of Privacy Programs, SpectraHealth
Attachments: Spectra_TIA_Scope.xlsx (spreadsheet), Subprocessor-Inventory_Spectra.csv (csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@spectrahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TIA scope and subprocessor carveouts – initial materials attached

Alyssa —

Got the files, thanks. Quick read-through and initial thoughts below; looping in Kimberly (legal) and Jonas (infra) to opine on the carveout and technical attestations. Laura — including you for procurement cadence.

High level proposal:
1) Treat SCCs + UK IDTA as Redwood's default standard for SpectraHealth hosted routes.
2) For the three APAC analytics subprocessors, accept a TIA carveout only if Spectra can provide: a recent SOC2-type attestation or ISO27001 cert, and a scoping statement limiting data types/processes.
3) We’ll run a 3-week evidence sprint: week 1 = documentation handoff & inventory validation; week 2 = infra attestations (residency, cache fallback design); week 3 = legal review + signoff.

Kimberly — can you add the minimum legal gating items and confirm whether an onshore-fallback clause is required in the DPA? Jonas — can your team produce a residency attestation PDF and a short note on KV-cache residency behavior?

Proposed milestones for Spectra procurement:
- 04/07: Redwood sends evidence checklist + redline (we’ll include a draft of SCCs redline)
- 04/16: Spectra uploads required evidence into shared Drive
- 04/23: Internal signoff for go/no-go

If that looks reasonable I’ll draft a mutual action plan doc and a short email for procurement.

Best,
Ben
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@spectrahealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TIA scope and subprocessor carveouts – initial materials attached

Ben / Alyssa —

I reviewed the TIA scope and the subprocessor inventory. High-level legal checklist below (these are minimums; we can expand if Spectra requires a bespoke onshore residency guarantee):

Legal gating items (minimum):
- Confirmed and signed Subprocessor CSV with contact and scope (we need to match names to the inventory rows). Please provide the Subprocessor-Inventory_Spectra.csv with signatures, or a cover letter from Spectra legal.
- For any carveout (APAC analytics): evidence of a third-party assurance (SOC2/ISO or equivalent) not older than 18 months, plus a written scoping statement that limits processing to pseudonymized telemetry only.
- Redline of SCCs + UK IDTA: I’ve attached a short draft redline (SCCs_UKIDTA_draft-redline.pdf). Please review and confirm any non-standard clauses Spectra needs.
- Residency fallback: if Spectra requires an onshore-cache fallback, we need explicit language in the DPA describing the activation trigger and proof of technical segregation (e.g., dedicated VPC or tenancy).
- KMS/HSM mapping: if Spectra will require independent key custody, provide KMS vendor, region, and whether keys are customer-managed.

Operational asks for infra (Jonas):
- Residenc y attestation PDF covering production region(s) and token KV-cache behavior during failover.
- A short note on logging and access controls for subprocessors so Spectra can evaluate evidence provenance.

Alyssa — once we have the signed CSV and the SOC/ISO docs for the carveout processors, Redwood legal can scope the carveout language quickly (we aim for a single paragraph carveout tethered to evidence).

Attaching: SCCs_UKIDTA_draft-redline.pdf (redline stub).

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy
Redwood Inference
Attachments: SCCs_UKIDTA_draft-redline.pdf (pdf)
